newsitem.title: USA: Parole denied to Bremer, who shot George Wallace.
newsitem.headline: Parole denied to Bremer, who shot George Wallace.

text.p: Arthur Bremer, who tried to assassinate Alabama Gov. George Wallace in 1972, was refused parole Friday and will remain in prison until at least 2015, according to a spokesman for the Maryland Parole Commission.
The parole commission cited reasons of public safety.
Bremer, 46, was sentenced to 53 years in prison for the shooting of Wallace, then a candidate for the Democratic presidential nomination. Wallace was making a campaign stop in Laurel, Maryland.

Wallace, now 72, was paralysed from the waist down and remains bedridden and in pain, according to his spokesman, David Azbell. He served four terms as Alabama governor and ran for presidfent four times.
He won over 13 percent of the vote as a third party candidate in 1968 and was considered a stronger candidate until he was shot in 1972.
"If I hadn't been shot out of the race, I would have been elected president," he said later. Neither constant pain nor impaired hearing kept him from winning the Alabama governorship again in 1974.

Bremer refused to participate in a parole hearing in 1985, the last time he was eligible, but requested consideration in March, 1996, said Leonard Sipes, spokesman for the Maryland Department of Public safety and Correctional Service.
The Commission heard his case in June and Friday released its decision that Bremer should be refused parole for public safety reasons.
Bremer is held at Maryland Correctional Institution in Hagerstown. He could have his sentence, due to run out on 2025, trimmed back 10 years for good behaviour, Sipes said.
